title: U.S. House · Florida's 21st District
area: The Treasure Coast and northern Palm Beach County, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.
Incumbent Rep. Brian Mast (R)'s Republican primary was canceled and he advanced unopposed. James Martin won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Bernard Taylor.
David Fabrikant is running as a write-in candidate with no party affiliation.

summary.text: Brian Mast is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for the 21st District, first elected in 2016. A U.S. Army veteran who served more than 12 years as a bomb disposal expert, he lost both legs to an improvised explosive device in Afghanistan. He chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee and also sits on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

background.text: Born and raised in Grand Rapids, Michigan, in 1980, according to Wikipedia; graduated from South Christian High School in 1999.
Attended Palm Beach Atlantic University, American Military University, and the Harvard University Extension School; Wikipedia reports a Bachelor of Liberal Arts from Harvard Extension School in 2016.

Served in the U.S. Army for more than 12 years, according to his official biography, earning the Bronze Star Medal, Army Commendation Medal for Valor, Purple Heart Medal, and Defense Meritorious Service Medal.
Worked as a bomb disposal expert under Joint Special Operations Command in Afghanistan; the last improvised explosive device he found cost him both legs. Wikipedia dates the injury to 2010.

Stayed on active duty during recovery and provided expertise to the National Nuclear Security Administration and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, then after retiring from the Army worked as an explosive specialist for the Department of Homeland Security.
According to his official biography, he volunteered alongside the Israel Defense Forces after earning his Harvard degree; Wikipedia dates this to January 2015.

Won the open 21st District seat in November 2016, defeating Democrat Randy Perkins, independent Carla Spalding, and write-in candidate Marilyn Holloman, after Rep. Patrick Murphy left to run for the U.S. Senate.

Now in his fifth term; chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee (since 2025) and serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, where his official biography lists Lake Okeechobee water quality among his priorities.
Lives in Fort Pierce with his wife, Brianna, and four children, according to his official biography. His August 2026 Republican primary was canceled and he advanced unopposed.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a strong supporter of Israel and says he has worked on the Foreign Affairs Committee to counter the BDS movement and support Israel's regional security efforts.
positions.quote: As a strong supporter of the state of Israel, I believe we must continue to repair the U.S. – Israel Relationship... As a member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, I have worked to oppose the dangerous BDS movement, support Israel's efforts to counter instability in the Middle East, and prevent a nuclear-armed Iran.

record.text: Serves as Chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and also sits on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee for the 2025–2026 Congress.
Says he opposed the Iran Nuclear Deal and voted for sanctions on Iran, North Korea, and Russia.

summary.text: James Martin is a U.S. Coast Guard veteran running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent Brian Mast. According to his campaign website, he grew up in Hobe Sound, graduated from the U.S. Coast Guard Academy, and served on active duty for nearly ten years, ending as a White House national security staff member. He is campaigning on cost of living, clean water, and anti-corruption measures.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Hobe Sound, Florida, where his family has lived since the early 1930s, and is a fourth-generation Floridian; his father runs Diamond Transfer & Garage, founded by his great-grandfather in 1934.
Attended Martin County Public Schools, including South Fork High School, according to his campaign website.
Earned an appointment to the U.S. Coast Guard Academy and says he graduated with honors in naval architecture and marine engineering.

Says he served on four Coast Guard ships, from Middle East combat zones to drug-trafficking lanes in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, and commanded two Coast Guard cutters in Fort Pierce for two years.

His campaign website says his last active-duty assignment was Chief of Staff for National Security Affairs and Executive Secretary of the Office of the Vice President at the White House from 2022 to 2025, serving Vice Presidents Harris and Vance.
Holds a commission as a lieutenant commander in the U.S. Coast Guard Reserve and is a life member of the Society of the Cincinnati, according to his campaign website.
Won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Bernard Taylor.

priorities.text: Says he opposes tariffs and supports using antitrust enforcement to address corporate consolidation driving up costs for working families.
Says he will work to complete Everglades restoration, clean up Lake Okeechobee, and stop toxic discharges into the St. Lucie Estuary and Indian River Lagoon.
Says he supports getting money out of politics, banning members of Congress from trading stocks, and closing the revolving door between Congress and lobbying.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariffs, saying they drive up grocery prices for working families.
Supports completing Everglades restoration and ending toxic discharges affecting Treasure Coast waterways, and says he will not compromise on environmental laws.

summary.text: Alexander Cooke is a former Juno Beach mayor and councilmember running without party affiliation for the 21st District. He describes himself as a fiscal conservative with over 20 years in investment management and trading, and campaigns on water quality, development, and housing and insurance costs.

background.text: Graduated from Curtis Senior High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Fairfield University in 2005, according to Ballotpedia.

Says he had his first job as an assistant to a maintenance worker at a low-income housing property in Washington state as a teenager, and that he lived in a car during his teenage years amid family difficulties.
Has worked as a financial executive, says he has over 20 years of experience in investment management and trading, and owns and runs Optimist Capital LLC in Palm Beach Gardens.
Served as Mayor and Councilmember of Juno Beach from 2022 to 2024, according to his survey responses.
Says he has a record of fighting overdevelopment and for the environment, and that he opposes spending taxpayer money on what he calls vanity projects.

priorities.text: Says he will focus on clean water and controlling Lake Okeechobee discharges, citing his experience as Juno Beach mayor.
Says he will focus on housing costs, property insurance, and cost-of-living stability, and opposes what he calls wasteful spending on projects such as the incumbent's support for renaming an airport.

summary.text: David Fabrikant is an attorney running as a write-in candidate with no party affiliation for the 21st District. He says he has practiced law for 25 years and spent the past 15 helping people with financial difficulties. His campaign materials list seven proposed laws.

background.text: Graduated from Hollywood Hills High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Florida in 1997, according to Ballotpedia.
Earned a law degree from St. Thomas University in 2000 and has worked as an attorney.
Says he has 25 years of legal experience, including 15 years helping people who are struggling with their finances.
Describes himself as a 50-year-old married father of two teenagers.
His Candidate Connection survey lists seven proposed laws he has drafted, including tying the minimum wage to congressional salaries and basing committee selection on seniority.

priorities.text: Says he has drafted seven proposed laws, including taxing ammunition and restricting certain weapons for civilian use, tying the minimum wage to congressional salaries, and requiring corporations to disclose what share of their workforce is AI.
Says his policy priorities include economic support for lower-income people, public health, children's access to food, access to healthcare, and vaccination.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for incumbent Brian Mast are added separately by script. James Martin has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions drawn from his campaign website. Alexander Cooke and David Fabrikant both completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; no FEC finance data is yet available for Fabrikant. Biographies rely on Ballotpedia, Mast's official site, and Martin's campaign 'Meet James' page; no campaign websites were found for Cooke or Fabrikant, and no Mast campaign site was reviewed.
